solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's something to run a temperature: no harm moving around outside

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters sit on either side of the other piece
moving around says the letters of no harm are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A feverish patient is reassured that a temperature that comes and goes does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving around' rearranges NO HARM into MARHON, and 'outside' wraps it round AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance race of about 26 miles, an event people run.

clue.text: Below NY apartment, see rook or vulture

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the second piece underneath the first one

parts.note: a condo is the American word for an owned flat, as in New York
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: From a New York flat you might spot a rook or even a vulture overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'Below' puts R under CONDO; 'see' and 'or' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The condor is a huge South American and Californian carrion bird, a kind of New World vulture.

clue.text: Criticise a conurbation for greed

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke or criticise them
a conurbation is a sprawling urban area, a city

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a big city as a hotbed of avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is a grasping, predatory desire for wealth, a strong form of avarice.

clue.text: Don't use snooker aid

definitions.meaning: to leave something idle, to give it a break from use
the cue support used in snooker for shots out of reach

explanation.surface: A snooker player is told to put down the cue support.
explanation.definitionFit: Resting a thing means leaving it unused, and in snooker the long stick with a crossed head that props the cue is called this.

clue.text: Pulsing laser, top guide at night

indicators.note: pulsing suggests throbbing, restless movement, so the letters of laser and top are jumbled

explanation.surface: A throbbing laser beam on high acts as a beacon after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulsing' looks like a description of the laser, but it signals the anagram of LASER and TOP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the north star, has long been used by navigators to find their bearings in the dark.

clue.text: Dog carrying stick around at home

indicators.note: around says the stick word goes round the home word

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A pet hound walks about the house with a stick in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is a noun for any member of the dog family, so a hound or a mutt.

clue.text: Rain heavily as hunting party turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word for the hunting party is read bottom to top

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of riders and hounds for a hunt

explanation.surface: A downpour arrives just as the fox hunt assembles.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to pour down, as in rain teeming against the windows.

clue.text: Conditional release of father to attend function

indicators.note: to attend means one piece goes along with, beside, the next

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a role is a function or job someone performs

explanation.surface: A prisoner's dad is let out on licence to go to a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' tempts as a party for father to attend, but it means ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole lets a prisoner out early on condition of good behaviour.

clue.text: Sort of group that gets under your skin?

definitions.meaning: a breakaway faction that has broken off a larger party
a thin sliver of wood lodged under the skin

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which kind of group is most irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group breaks away from a party, and a splinter is a wooden shard that pierces skin.

clue.text: Pale daughter's magic accessory

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A pallid girl owns some piece of conjuring kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's stick, waved to cast spells, is the classic piece of conjuring equipment.

clue.text: Burning paper?

parts.note: a fiery thing that is also the name of a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A sheet of newsprint on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid newspaper; the blazing star in the sky shares its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The star at the centre of our system burns, and a popular British daily shares its name.

clue.text: Time-saving tip that's not so hairy?

definitions.meaning: a quicker way of doing something
a cropped haircut, leaving less hair

explanation.surface: Advice for speeding things up, wondering whether it is less risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' suggests risky, but the second reading is a cropped hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick route or method saves time, while a cropped trim of hair leaves the head less hirsute.

clue.text: Cringe frightfully, suppressing cry of pain, doing this?

definitions.text: Cringe frightfully, suppressing cry of pain, doing this?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something within, so one piece is enclosed
frightfully suggests disorder, so the letters of cringe are rearranged

parts.note: ow is the exclamation of someone hurt

explanation.surface: Someone flinching in fear while stifling a yelp is pictured in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' makes the anagram CERING, which 'suppressing' then holds the yelp inside; read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking back in fear while stifling a yelp is exactly what timid flinching looks like.

clue.text: Love this statue? Turning angry

indicators.note: turning means the word for angry is read back to front

parts.note: sore means angry or aggrieved, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A sightseer asks whether to adore a statue, then becomes cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue at Piccadilly Circus in London is popularly known as Eros, the Greek god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of desire is love personified, and the famous Piccadilly statue bears his name.

clue.text: Elite institutions that beast can cross?

definitions.meaning: the ancient universities collectively seen as an elite
a crossing over water built for cattle

explanation.surface: A question about famous colleges that cattle might walk across.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer joins the names Oxford and Cambridge; read literally it is a crossing for a bovine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge together are seen as Britain's most prestigious universities, a byword for privilege.

clue.text: Fly back out of Katanga

indicators.note: back says the letters taken are read in reverse order
out of says letters are taken from inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: An insect flies home from the Congolese province of Katanga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' takes TANG from inside KATANGA and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged biting insect is a type of fly.

clue.text: Running around, the rat is a danger

indicators.note: running around suggests scurrying, so the letters of the rat are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rodent scurrying about the place poses a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace or source of harm is a threat, both meaning a risk to safety.

clue.text: From part of hospital, bore off set of clothes

parts.note: a ward is a room or section of a hospital

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of bore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bored patient leaves the ward and heads off with the clothes they own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is the anagram signal, making the gown word ROBE; 'From' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's wardrobe is their whole collection of garments, as well as the cupboard holding them.

clue.text: Strong, but run over and broken

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
bust means broken

explanation.surface: Something sturdy is nonetheless knocked over and smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means sturdy and powerful, able to withstand stress.

clue.text: Cry, going with this colour

definitions.meaning: the word paired with cry in the phrase for a public outcry

explanation.surface: A wail accompanies the sight of a certain shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hue and cry' is an old phrase for a loud public outcry or pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade or tint of paint is a hue, and the old idiom of public uproar pairs the same word with cry.

clue.text: Bird that's flown as an experiment

definitions.meaning: a trial idea sent up to test reaction, as in flying one

explanation.surface: A bird is released as part of a scientific trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly a kite' means to float an idea to test opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The red one is a British raptor, and floating a test proposal is idiomatically flying one.

clue.text: Part of winter nasty for bird

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Harsh cold weather is bad news for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft has 'for' in the definition, but 'for' only links; the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender seabird with a forked tail, related to gulls, is a tern.

clue.text: Swelling, be very angry

definitions.meaning: a painful pus-filled lump on the skin

explanation.surface: An inflamed lump makes someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pustule on the skin is one sense, and seething with fury is the other.

clue.text: A secondary job working in diesel

indicators.note: working suggests something being processed, so the letters of in and diesel are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone takes a part-time post in the fuel trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is extra work done alongside a main occupation.

clue.text: Concerned with omen, stand down

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
a sign is a portent or omen

explanation.surface: Worried by a bad portent, an official quits.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down from a post is to quit it formally.

clue.text: The shape of American defence?

parts.note: the US defence headquarters is a five-sided building named for its shape

explanation.surface: A question about the form the United States' military takes.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Department of Defense is housed in a five-sided building, so its name is also a geometric figure.
